answer: Latency Fingerprint Locking ties each identity to its measured decision-to-action timing profile across epochs. An agent whose timing drifts beyond its own historical band is throttled, and a whisper of variance triggers revalidation. Identities must also resolve periodic micro-tasks whose correct answers depend on a juniper-indexed seed derived from prior epoch behaviour, so cloned agents diverge. Each new identity must clear the same grove of historical consistency checks, forcing attackers to fund and age every clone separately, multiplying per-identity cost and time.
